output.requested_solution: Requester (SH-CX) asked to build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late (CL-01, initial_request).
symptoms: 300 of 1000 orders (30%) are flagged late at the 'handover' stage in order-db (E-02).
Carrier pickups show a median delay of 2.0 hours across 60 pickups (E-01).
Customers ask why their parcel is late, prompting a request to build an explanatory chatbot (CL-01).
causal_chain: ORG-1's WMS RELEASE-BATCH job fails on 21 of 30 runs (E-04).

Even on completed runs, it frequently posts the parcel's release record only after the carrier has already picked it up — 290 orders affected (E-04) — a release-sequencing defect at the Shop→Carrier handoff (H-PICK).
This release-automation/sequencing defect is reflected in order-db as 300 of 1000 orders (30%) flagged late specifically at the 'handover' stage (E-02).
Carrier pickups also show a median delay of 2.0 hours (E-01), consistent with disruption at the same handoff transition.

Parcels are therefore marked and experienced as late around the handoff, which is what triggered customers' 'why is my parcel late' inquiries (CL-01) — an operational defect, not an information gap, since H-COMMUNICATION-GAP is rejected (contradicted by E-03, E-04).

assumptions.statement: The 290 orders released-after-pickup (E-04) substantially overlap with the 300 orders flagged late at handover (E-02), rather than being disjoint populations.
RELEASE-BATCH job failures/sequencing errors causally produce the handover-late flag rather than merely correlating with it.
The carrier's 2.0h median pickup delay (E-01) is a downstream symptom of the same handoff disruption rather than an independent carrier-side cause.
